MC	<p>55a2_b832</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mxy, +++, mxy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b305_0900</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7b5700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bek, +++, bek"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a7e2_fea6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhr, +++, dhr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697b;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dky, +++, dky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6652_94d9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hkw, +++, hkw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>42e2_6526</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abm, +++, abm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5602_364f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ent, +++, ent"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9aea_65d7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kmn, +++, kmn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4be4_ddb3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7b5700;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697b;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fht, +++, fht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7b5700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bty, +++, bty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8b71_20c4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bfy, +++, bfy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b637_336a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fwx, +++, fwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5fc1_9a35</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5eaa;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1b5eaa;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8959_ca6d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6e41af;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dnr, +++, dnr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>031a_b757</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhx, +++, dhx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c425_ff7c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdn, +++, bdn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5b2a_d7bb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bht, +++, bht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0c6a_a750</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, apx, +++, apx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b527_8f1f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7f4d_fcf9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7b5700;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9a2d6e;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhp, +++, fhp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>227c_9a89</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhx, +++, fhx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3573_914e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9a2d6e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, anw, +++, anw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d47a_f2ec</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dfn, +++, dfn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4c76_991f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e41af;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>bf9b_0095</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7b5700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bfn, +++, bfn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>275e_a161</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9a2d6e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajn, +++, ajn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7ee9_3a85</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kry, +++, kry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6051_e617</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fjp, +++, fjp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d1a6_8365</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6e41af;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jmr, +++, jmr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cem, +++, cem"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>be13_d9cf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5eaa;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1b5eaa;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5eaa;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, atw, +++, atw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1833_f7ae</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6e41af;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hnt, +++, hnt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>337b_73c6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6e41af;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efw, +++, efw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>228a_e553</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7b5700;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7b5700;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dft, +++, dft"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
