MC	<p>2538_4e50</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9a2d6e;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ade, +++, ade"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993845;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #993845;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993845;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhp, +++, fhp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bf7f_c347</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9a2d6e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdf, +++, cdf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>56ba_7528</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6e41af;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kry, +++, kry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b531_f661</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekx, +++, ekx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2e5b_5940</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176b68;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #176b68;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176b68;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhj, +++, dhj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a825_52d9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #695f00;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #695f00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #695f00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697b;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cef, +++, cef"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d118_4984</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5eaa;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b5eaa;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>4778_05c6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697b;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mnr, +++, mnr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>441c_1233</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hpx, +++, hpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884d13;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d13;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296e35;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #296e35;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296e35;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #823f8a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #823f8a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bce, +++, bce"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ae65_f2fa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697b;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00697b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abe, +++, abe"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4d0b_7b22</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206589;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #206589;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206589;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9a2d6e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2d6e;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ahj, +++, ahj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1bf5_4725</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3b19;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3b19;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #086e54;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #086e54;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #086e54;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #484fbd;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #484fbd;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehn, +++, ehn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>822d_57ed</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4e6906;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e6906;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697b;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e41af;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e41af;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 16px;"><div style="min-width: 0; max-width: 100%;"><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abk, +++, abk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
